title: Predictive Prefill Throttler + Adaptive Kernel Coster to Cut Host Overhead
creator: Asha Banerjee
description:
Problem: Host CPU tail latency and cycles spent in prefill/decode orchestration are a top contributor to per-token cost for our hosted tier. Observed sources: overly conservative prefill batching, kernel mis-selection for short/long sequences, frequent small pinned-memory memcpy operations, and threadpool contention from mixed-priority requests.

Goal: Reduce end-to-end host overhead (CPU cycles and memory copy spikes) for mixed workloads by introducing a predictive prefill throttler that shapes prefill submission based on token-deadlines and a Bayesian adaptive kernel coster that predicts kernel runtimes and selects kernels to minimize combined host+device latency. Target: 20-35% host CPU reduction on 95th-percentile latencies for multi-tenant workloads and 10-15% cost-per-token improvement in hosted steady-state traffic.
acceptance_criteria: New throttler deployed behind feature-flag that reduces host CPU consumption by >=20% on our production load replay for 95th latency without increasing GPU utilization by more than 5%.
Adaptive kernel coster achieves >=10% decrease in average kernel mis-selection compared to baseline model-hint selector on A/B traffic split.
No regression on correctness: identical token outputs within tolerances when switching kernel variants for same model/inputs.
Threadpool preemption controls prevent low-priority bulk prefill from inflating high-priority decode latency (measured in per-route dashboards).
Comprehensive dashboards (Console) showing before/after host CPU, memcpy rates, kernel selection distribution, and tail latency for routes under flag.
notes: 2026-02-22: Spike completed. Benchmarked three approaches: reactive windowing, fixed microbatching, and predictive deadline-aware throttling. Predictive approach gave best trade-off for mixed short and long sequences.

2026-02-27: PoC of Bayesian kernel coster implemented. Uses lightweight online feature vector (seq_len, kv_cache_hits, model_variant, device_temp_est) and updates cost posterior every 5s. Initial priors from historical traces.
2026-03-03: Integration test showed memcpy burst reduction by batching pin/unpin operations into slab lifetimes. Implemented a pin slab allocator in host arena to avoid repeated page-lock churn.

2026-03-05: Observed that threadpool starvation still occurs when many low-priority prefill tasks flood the work queue. Added soft-isolation via QoS queues with eBPF-based cgroup tagging to steer syscalls; promising in canary.
2026-03-08: Security review noted potential info leak in kernel cost telemetry. We agreed to aggregate metrics to per-route buckets and redaction for customer IDs.
2026-03-10: Canary rollout to 5% traffic for routes serving chat-short and chat-long. Early telemetry: host CPU down 18% P95, memcpy operations down 28%, kernel mis-selections down 12%.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Li): please add a metric to ensure no tail regressions >2x for single-tenant high-priority customers during canary.
Infra (Nina Patel): NUMA-aware slab allocator needs a fallback for instances without hugepages; suggested per-socket arenas.
Performance (Liam O'Connor): Bayesian model should include 'active_batch_size' to better predict kernel scaling behavior under batching.
Security (Maya Singh): aggregate kernel telemetry is fine, avoid logging device serials.

implementation_decisions: Use deadline-aware scheduling: assign each request a soft-deadline computed from route SLA and token budget; prefill submissions are delayed if predicted GPU start would miss deadline.
Bayesian kernel coster chosen over deterministic heuristics because it adapts online to device thermal/drift and model quantization differences.
Host slab allocator reused across prefill/decode to amortize page-lock costs; slabs are per-NUMA socket and reclaimed aggressively on pressure.
Threadpool uses three lanes: realtime (decode, high-priority), interactive (short-prefill), batch (bulk prefill). Worker affinity and lane quotas prevent cross-lane contention.
Feature-flag rollout with telemetry gates and automatic rollback on regression.
Avoid storing per-request kernel decision logs to persistent store; only aggregate counts and latency histograms are exported.
risks: Incorrect deadline predictions could increase GPU idle time (wasted capacity) or harm tail latency for high-priority requests.
Bayesian updater may be slow to adapt for cold-start models; mitigation: bootstrap priors from archived traces and conservative fallback to default kernels.
NUMA slab allocator may increase memory footprint if not tuned; mitigation: dynamic slab sizing and cross-socket steals under pressure.
QoS lane misconfiguration could starve batch work causing throughput loss; add auto-tuning heuristics and safety caps.
